title: wespa's embedding contract is proved by a CI host fixture
description: A same-origin test-host fixture served by the viewer's dev server (route `/test-host.html` behind a `--test-host` flag or an env guard; off by default so wespa's proxy allow-list is unaffected) mimics the wespa shell: a 56px header, a resizable sidebar (64px collapsed, 200-400px expanded, user-resizable live via a drag handle), a content pane carrying an `<iframe src="./?embed=1&theme=light">`. The host posts `{ type: "rcf-view-theme", theme: "light"|"dark" }` on a toggle control; it stores no theme itself so a passing run proves the iframe reads the message. The viewer sends no outbound postMessage. Three lints run in the test suite: (1) framing lint (`GET /` returns no `X-Frame-Options`, no CSP `frame-ancestors` that forbids same-origin, and the fixture loads the iframe without a browser error); (2) target lint (no `target="_top"` string in the server-rendered HTML); (3) localStorage namespace lint (every `localStorage.{setItem,getItem,removeItem}` and shared `storage.*` call site in `src/view/**` uses a key starting with `rcf-view:v1:`). Amended 2026-10-04 (w-2026-10-04-dave-001): the viewer's own three-state theme control (Light|Dark|Auto) sits right of the SearchButton in non-embed mode, is hidden entirely under `embed=1` and in non-embed mode persists its setting under `rcf-view:v1:theme` per ADR-4137 (Dave's storage ruling 2026-10-04). See viewer UI refresh design doc section 9 and section 11 recommendation 6, and Dex's wespa requirements of 2026-10-02.
asA: Dex integrating the rcf-lite viewer behind wespa's reverse proxy
iWant: a CI host fixture that proves the viewer honours the embedding contract and three lints that keep framing, target='_top' and localStorage namespace in place over time; and a visible three-state theme control in the standalone viewer that is hidden under embed=1
soThat: regressions in the embedding contract are caught in the viewer's own suite before they reach wespa, and standalone viewer users can switch theme without a URL edit

acceptanceCriteria.description: [happy] Given the test-host fixture at `/test-host.html`, when the page loads with the viewer served from the same origin, then the iframe `src` is `./?embed=1&theme=light`, the title block and footer of the iframed viewer are hidden (`<html data-embed="1">`), the tab nav is visible and the host's 56px header plus the resizable sidebar render around it.

[happy] Given the test-host fixture with the iframe loaded, when the host's theme toggle posts `{ type: "rcf-view-theme", theme: "dark" }` to the iframe's `contentWindow`, then the iframe's `<html data-theme>` flips to `dark` without a reload and the content repaints in the dark token set.

[happy] Given the test-host fixture with the iframe loaded at `./?embed=1&theme=dark`, when a hash-only navigation inside the iframe writes `#tab=requirements&entity=REQ-002`, then the iframe's query still carries `embed=1` and `theme=dark` and the viewer's inner `<html data-embed="1" data-theme="dark">` is preserved.

[failure] Given the viewer page listening for `rcf-view-theme` postMessages, when a message with `event.origin` different from `window.location.origin` is delivered, then the message is ignored and `<html data-theme>` is not changed.

[must-not] Given the viewer's `GET /` response, when the three lints run in the test suite, then (a) no `X-Frame-Options` header is set and no CSP `frame-ancestors` directive forbids same-origin framing, (b) `target="_top"` appears zero times in the rendered HTML across every tab, (c) every `localStorage.{setItem,getItem,removeItem}` and shared `storage.*` call site under `src/view/**` uses a key starting with `rcf-view:v1:`.

[must-not] Given the test-host fixture and the viewer page, when either is loaded, then neither posts any outbound message beyond the host's `rcf-view-theme`; the viewer sends no `postMessage` of any shape, and the test-host adds no new postMessage shape.

[happy] Given the standalone viewer loaded without `embed=1`, when the shell paints, then a three-state theme control (`role="group"`, three buttons Light|Dark|Auto with `aria-pressed`) renders in the header's `.tools` group right of the SearchButton; when a button is pressed, `<html data-theme>` is set to `light` or `dark` (or the attribute is removed for Auto so the `prefers-color-scheme` media query decides) live without a reload, and the pressed button's `aria-pressed` becomes `true` while the others become `false`.

[happy] Given the standalone (non-embed) viewer, when a theme button is pressed, then the chosen value (`light`, `dark` or `auto`) is written to `localStorage['rcf-view:v1:theme']`; on the next page load the stored value is reapplied; the boot precedence is `?theme=` wins first, then the stored value, then the default (`auto`); and the postMessage `rcf-view-theme` listener still applies live but writes nothing to the stored key.

[must-not] Given the viewer loaded with `?embed=1`, when the shell paints, then the three-state theme control is absent from the DOM entirely (no `[data-rcf-theme-control]` element rendered, not merely hidden by CSS), and no read or write of `localStorage['rcf-view:v1:theme']` happens on load, on a postMessage theme change, or on any user action inside the viewer.

[happy] Given the standalone viewer with a stored value `rcf-view:v1:theme = dark`, when the URL carries `?theme=light`, then on load `<html data-theme>` is `light` (the explicit query wins) and the Light button is pressed; the stored value is left as `dark` and is reused on the next load without a `?theme=` query.
